description_html:
Our mission and customers: We are creating the freedom for SMEs to succeed by delivering Europe's leading finance workspace with banking at its core, augmented by financial tools. We are proud to be rated 4.8 on Trustpilot, based on 55,000+ reviews. Our culture puts customer satisfaction at the core of what we do, as proven by our Net Promoter Score of 75 (more about our culture here).

Our journey: Founded in 2017 by Alexandre and Steve, Qonto has grown to 1,600+ Qontoers serving over 600,000+ customers across 8 European countries. We have been profitable since 2023, and we are just getting started.

Our beliefs: We hire for skills and potential. With 80+ nationalities, 45% women, of which 56% of women in our leadership team, diversity isn't a program; It's who we are. We've built a discrimination-free hiring process because the best teams are built on merit.

AI at Qonto: AI is deeply embedded in how we work (here) - Every Qontoer gets unlimited access to the best AI tools. We want people who experiment without waiting for permission, push AI beyond the obvious, know when to trust it, and when to question it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Location: You can choose to work at Qonto as long as you're living in (or willing to relocate to) either Germany, France, Italy, Serbia, Portugal, or Spain.

➡️ Mission

Join us as an Android Engineer and help us build the mobile experience that 600,000+ European businesses rely on every day to manage their finances. You'll own product-critical features end-to-end — from technical design to rollout — in a large, modular Kotlin codebase where craft and velocity both matter. You'll work closely with Product, Design, Backend, and Frontend.

➡️ What you'll do

  • Own features end-to-end: You'll take ownership from discovery and technical design through implementation, rollout, and iteration on features that help businesses pay, get paid, and stay in control.
  • Drive technical decisions in your squad: You'll shape solutions with Product, Design, and Backend by clarifying tradeoffs across UX, performance, security, and time-to-market.
  • Raise app reliability and maintainability: You'll improve architecture, performance, and test strategy to scale the app without compromising stability.
  • Tackle complex mobile challenges: You'll contribute to real-time synchronization, resilience patterns, and smooth navigation in a modular codebase with ~1,000 modules.
  • Grow the team's Android craft: You'll lead code reviews and technical discussions, share patterns, and mentor peers to raise the bar on quality and delivery.

➡️ What we're looking for

  • Strong Android native experience: You've shipped and maintained production features with Kotlin and are comfortable owning technical decisions end-to-end.
  • Quality-driven mindset: You care about testing (unit, UI, snapshot), clean code, and pragmatic standards that keep teams moving fast.
  • Problem-solving approach: You thrive in ambiguity and turn complex constraints into simple, robust solutions.
  • AI-native workflow: You use AI coding tools daily to amplify your output — not just experiment with them.
  • Collaborative by nature: You're fluent in English and contribute through code reviews, knowledge sharing, and mentorship across technical and non-technical stakeholders.

➡️ What we can offer you

  • An AI-first engineering environment: Unlimited access to Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot — and a culture that expects you to use them to raise the bar, not just go faster (click here to read our vision statement on AI)
  • Engineering standards that scale: Strong code review culture, continuous refactoring, and a focus on correctness in a regulated context.
  • A technically demanding domain: Fintech constraints — security, compliance, real-time data — push you to solve problems most mobile engineers never encounter.

➡️ Our methodology, the Qonto Way

  • We value upfront technical design, team reviews, and smart slicing — quality drives the velocity our customers need.
  • Our org assigns one team lead per project across stacks, giving your team a clear mission and full autonomy on how it operates.
  • Our lean toolbox, Kaizen and PDCA, lets you monitor and drive continuous improvement collaboratively with your peers and manager.
Want to go further? Click here

➡️ Our stack & practices

  • Kotlin-first & modern concurrency: 100% Kotlin codebase with Coroutines + Flow throughout.
  • Architecture: MVVM + Clean Architecture with modular design (~1000 modules).
  • UI direction: New screens built with Jetpack Compose, with a large share of legacy views already migrated.
  • CI/CD & quality: GitHub Actions, Bitrise, Firebase Test Lab, Sonar, Fastlane.
  • Testing culture: 26k+ unit tests, 14k+ snapshot tests, 500+ UI tests.

Curious about how we tackle tech debt? Check out our talk from the last Droidcon here featuring Florian.

➡️ Your future team

As an Android Engineer, you will join one of Qonto's squad teams, each organised around a clear project mission, with one team lead and full ownership of a product scope. You'll be part of a 140+ mobile engineering community within a 500+ Product Engineering department, working in focused teams of 5 to 10 people alongside Product, Design, and peers from Frontend and Backend.

At Qonto, we understand that true diversity isn’t just about ticking boxes on a hiring checklist. Apply regardless of the boxes you tick — who knows? You may have the missing piece of the puzzle we’ve been searching for all along.
 
By applying, you agree that Qonto processes your personal data to assess your application. Your data is kept for up to 2 years in our candidate pool. Read our Privacy Notice for full details.

On average, our hiring process lasts 20 working days. More information on our candidate journey here

Recruitment scams are on the rise. Keep in mind, we will never work with third-party platforms or agencies that request payment from candidates.

Wie dein Alltag aussehen wird?

Tja, gar nicht so leicht zu beantworten, denn deine Aufgaben sind abwechslungsreich und immer unterschiedlich. Aber in der Regel wirst du die Möglichkeit haben, unsere Strategie zur Lead-Generierung mitzugestalten, jeden Monat Zielbranchen auszuwählen und unsere Outreach-Aktivitäten voranzutreiben.

Bei Odoo schätzen wir deine Fähigkeiten mehr als den Lebenslauf.

Tasks

About the Role

We are looking for a IT Project Manager as freelancer to support the development and improvement of business applications and systems within a banking and financial services environment.

You will work closely with business stakeholders, developers, product teams, and external providers to analyze requirements, document processes, and ensure that systems meet business needs.

  • Act as a bridge between business and technical teams.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience as a Systems Analyst, Business Analyst, or similar role.
  • Strong requirements gathering and process analysis skills.
  • Experience with workflows, process mapping, and system documentation.
  • Good understanding of web applications, APIs, integrations, and data flows.
  • Experience with system testing and User Acceptance Testing.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Experience with tools such as Jira, Confluence, Visio, Miro, Lucidchart, or Draw.io is an advantage.

  • Currently, a Deutschlandticket (Germany-wide public transport pass)

  • An international environment with a dynamic, committed, and collaborative team

  • A secure position at a company that has built a consistent track record of success since its foundation in 2011

If you are motivated and excited about taking on this responsible role and becoming part of our success story, we encourage you to apply today!

We look forward to hearing from you!

title: Research Consultant (m/w/d)
salary_basis: Based on engineering benchmarks at Glasford International Deutschland GmbH
description_html:
Wer wir sind

Glasford International Deutschland (GID) ist eine national und international erfolgreich

agierende Personalberatung mit 35-jähriger Erfahrung in der Personalsuche und -

auswahl. Mit 25 Partnerbüros weltweit unterstützen wir Unternehmen bei der Suche

und Auswahl von geeigneten Führungskräften vornehmlich in den Fokusbranchen

Industrial Manufacturing, Technology und Consumer Goods. Langeweile ist bei uns

ein Fremdwort, Eigeninitiative und die Übernahme von Verantwortung werden

ausdrücklich gefördert; Spaß an der Arbeit betrachten wir als Grundlage für gute

Leistungen.

Aufgaben

Teilzeit oder Werkstudent | 20/25 Stunden pro Woche | München

Für die Unterstützung unseres Teams an unserem Hauptsitz im Herzen von München suchen wir ab sofort einen Research Consultant (m/w/d) in Teilzeit oder als Werkstudent.

In dieser Rolle unterstützt du unsere Berater bei der Bearbeitung laufender Suchmandate und erhältst einen umfassenden Einblick in die Arbeit einer Personalberatung. Dein Schwerpunkt liegt auf Research, der Identifikation geeigneter Kandidaten sowie deren individueller Ansprache und Kommunikation.

Nach einer gründlichen Einarbeitung übernimmst du eigenständig definierte Aufgaben innerhalb unserer Mandate und arbeitest eng mit unseren Beratern und dem Management zusammen. Dabei erhältst du Einblicke in unterschiedliche Unternehmen, Märkte und Positionen und entwickelst zunehmend ein Gespür für passende Kandidatenprofile.

Deine Aufgaben

Zu deinen Aufgaben gehören insbesondere:

  • Recherche und Identifikation potenziell geeigneter Kandidaten für unsere Suchmandate
  • Analyse relevanter Unternehmen, Märkte und Kandidatenprofile
  • Erstellung und Pflege von Zielfirmenlisten, Longlists und Kandidatenübersichten
  • Aktive und individuelle Ansprache potenzieller Kandidaten über verschiedene Recruitingkanäle
  • Kommunikation mit Kandidaten während des laufenden Prozesses sowie Koordination weiterer Schritte
  • Strukturierte Aufbereitung von Research Ergebnissen und Kandidateninformationen für unsere Berater
  • Unterstützung bei der Vorbereitung und Organisation laufender Suchprojekte
  • Koordination und Vereinbarung von Gesprächsterminen zwischen Kandidaten und Beratern
  • Pflege und Aktualisierung von Kandidaten und Projektinformationen in unserem CRM Tool
  • Dokumentation des Projektfortschritts und regelmäßige Abstimmung mit den zuständigen Beratern
  • Teilnahme an Projektbriefings und regelmäßigen Teammeetings

Der Schwerpunkt deiner Rolle liegt zunächst auf Research, Kandidatenidentifikation und Kandidatenkommunikation. Mit zunehmender Erfahrung kannst du schrittweise weitere Aufgaben innerhalb des Recruitingprozesses übernehmen und dich fachlich weiterentwickeln.

Qualifikation

Das bringst du mit

Uns ist weniger wichtig, an welchem Punkt deines beruflichen Weges du gerade stehst. Entscheidend ist, dass du Lust hast, dich in neue Themen einzuarbeiten und unser Team zuverlässig zu unterstützen.

Idealerweise:

  • studierst du aktuell oder suchst eine Teilzeitposition mit einem Umfang von etwa 20 bis 25 Stunden pro Woche
  • interessierst du dich für Recruiting, Personalberatung, Unternehmen und unterschiedliche Märkte
  • arbeitest du gerne strukturiert, sorgfältig und zuverlässig
  • hast du Freude an Recherche und daran, Informationen systematisch aufzubereiten
  • verfügst du über eine schnelle Auffassungsgabe und kannst dich gut in neue Themen einarbeiten
  • bringst du Eigeninitiative mit und organisierst deine Aufgaben selbstständig
  • gehst du sicher mit MS Office um
  • verfügst du über gute Englischkenntnisse und kannst englischsprachige Profile und Informationen sicher verstehen

Studiengänge wie Wirtschaftspsychologie, Betriebswirtschaftslehre, Psychologie, Personalmanagement oder vergleichbare Fachrichtungen können dir den Einstieg erleichtern, sind für uns aber keine Voraussetzung.

Vorkenntnisse im Recruiting oder Research sind ebenfalls nicht erforderlich. Wichtiger sind für uns Neugier, Lernbereitschaft und ein hoher Qualitätsanspruch an die eigene Arbeit.

Benefits

Das bieten wir dir

  • Eine Position mit etwa 20 bis 25 Stunden pro Woche, die sich gut mit einem Studium oder anderen Verpflichtungen kombinieren lässt
  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten und mobiles Arbeiten
  • Feste Homeoffice Möglichkeiten sowie zusätzliche Flexibilität nach Absprache
  • Eine gründliche Einarbeitung und einen direkten Einblick in die Arbeit einer etablierten Personalberatung
  • Abwechslungsreiche Suchprojekte und Einblicke in unterschiedliche Unternehmen, Märkte und Positionen
  • Die Möglichkeit, schnell eigene Aufgabenbereiche zu übernehmen
  • Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten innerhalb des Research und perspektivisch auch in weitere Bereiche des Recruitingprozesses
  • Flache Hierarchien und eine offene Duz Kultur
  • Kurze Entscheidungswege und ein hilfsbereites, engagiertes Team
  • Moderne und repräsentative Büroräume in zentraler Lage im Münchner Lehel
  • Und für die Mittagspause liegt der Eisbach praktisch direkt vor der Tür

Interesse?

Wenn du gerne recherchierst, strukturiert arbeitest und Lust hast, die Personalberatung von Grund auf kennenzulernen, freuen wir uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

Schick uns einfach deine aussagekräftigen Bewerbungsunterlagen und erzähl uns kurz, warum die Position für dich interessant ist.

title: Client Solutions Director / Solution Design Architect
salary_basis: Based on leadership compensation records at OLIVER Agency
description_html:
Established in 2004, OLIVER is the world's first and only specialist in designing, building, and running bespoke in-house agencies and marketing ecosystems for brands. We partner with over 300 clients in 40+ countries and counting. Our unique model drives creativity and efficiency, allowing us to deliver tailored solutions that resonate deeply with audiences. 

As a part of The Brandtech Group, we're at the forefront of leveraging cutting-edge AI technology to revolutionise how we create and deliver work. Our AI solutions enhance efficiency, spark creativity, and drive insightful decision-making, empowering our teams to produce innovative and impactful results. 

Solution Design Architect (AI / Transformation / Creative Operations)

Language requirement: fluency in German or Spanish

Location: Germany (primarily remote) and regular business travel across EMEA

Employment: 18-month FTC with view to extend

About the role: 

We're hiring a Solution Design Architect to help us win and shape new business. You'll sit in the room with senior client stakeholders, including CMOs, and turn their challenges into operating models, workflows and commercial models (team shapes, asset rates, outcome-based structures) that we can deliver. You'll bring the commercial judgement to validate the numbers, the process thinking to design better ways of working, and the technical and channel knowledge to lead the conversation when specialists aren't there. Quick on your feet and calm under pressure, you'll be supported by our Commercial and Implementation teams.

Key Responsibilities:

New Business and Client Engagement

  • Lead the operational and solution design element of new client pitches, presenting with credibility and confidence to senior client stakeholders, including CMOs and marketing leadership.
  • Formulate solutions in real time during pitches, workshops and challenging client discussions, staying composed and commercially sharp.
  • Own the conversation on technology and data when technical specialists aren't present, and know when and how to bring them in.
  • Ensure a smooth handover from pitch to implementation, so what we sell is what we deliver.

Requirement Gathering and Analysis

  • Work with stakeholders to gather, document and analyse business requirements for new client accounts.
  • Ask the right questions to define accurate scope, cost and risk.
  • Translate client business needs into workflows for client and technology teams.

Operating Model and Solution Design

  • Define and articulate operating model principles (roles, governance, ways of working, handoffs) that align to client goals and our delivery capability.
  • Evaluate existing client and internal processes, identify new ways of working, and recommend improvements for efficiency, cost reduction and better outcomes.
  • Design solutions across advertising and marketing channels, drawing on a strong understanding of how media, data, creative and technology fit together.
  • Collaborate with technology and business teams to ensure solutions align with our strategy and are technically feasible.

Commercial Modelling

  • Build, test and validate commercial models that deliver the designed workflow, including team shapes, asset-based rate models and outcome-based models.
  • Work with Commercial and Finance to pressure-test assumptions, margins and risk before models go to clients.
  • Balance client value with commercial viability, and explain the reasoning clearly to both internal and client audiences.

Stakeholder Communication

  • Act as the bridge between clients, commercial, technology and delivery teams, ensuring shared understanding and alignment.
  • Translate complex technical and commercial concepts into clear, compelling narratives for non-technical, senior audiences.

Data, Measurement and Reporting

  • Analyse data to support decision-making, and define measurement frameworks for new clients.
  • Create reports and presentations that convey findings and recommendations with clarity and impact.

About You:

Essential

  • 10-15 years' experience in solution design, consulting, strategy, operations or a similar role within advertising, marketing, media or marketing technology.
  • A confident, articulate communicator with a track record of presenting to and influencing C-suite and senior marketing stakeholders (CMOs or equivalent).
  • Commercial acumen, with hands-on experience building and validating pricing or commercial models (e.g. resourcing/team-shape models, rate cards, outcome-based or performance-linked structures).
  • A process-driven mindset, able to map, challenge and redesign ways of working and articulate clear operating model principles.
  • Strong working knowledge of advertising and marketing channels (e.g. paid media, social, programmatic, search, CRM, creative production) and how they connect to data and technology.
  • Enough technical fluency in martech, adtech, data and platforms to hold credible conversations with clients and lead when technical specialists aren't in the room.
  • Quick-thinking and resilient, comfortable formulating answers and options in high-pressure or contentious situations while maintaining client confidence.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to turn data into insight and recommendations.
  • Willingness and flexibility to travel regularly for client pitches, mostly across Europe and occasionally further afield.

Desirable

  • Experience contributing to new business wins, RFPs and pitch processes.
  • Experience in an agency, consultancy or in-house marketing transformation environment.
  • Experience with global or multi-market clients and remote, cross-functional teams.

What Success Looks Like:

  • Contribute directly to new business wins and improve pitch win rates.
  • Commercial models that are profitable, credible to clients and deliverable in practice.
  • Smooth transitions from pitch to implementation with no gap between what was sold and what is delivered.
  • Trusted by clients, commercial and technology teams as the go-to person for solution design.

title: AI Engineer (f/m/d)
salary_basis: Based on engineering benchmarks at Clariness
description_html:
Clariness is looking for an AI Engineer (f/m/d/) based in Germany.
- Full-time; unlimited -

About the role:

This role is about turning AI and machine learning ideas into reliable, scalable solutions for Clariness' platforms. You will join a collaborative technical environment and work across the AI/ML lifecycle, from understanding a business problem and developing a solution to deployment, monitoring and continuous improvement within the regulated clinical-trial space.

As an AI Engineer, you would be responsible for:

  • Designing, building and operating production AI and machine learning solutions, including data pipelines, models and inference services.
  • Developing LLM-powered features using approaches such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agent workflows, tool calling and structured outputs, with a focus on reliability, measurable quality and cost efficiency.
  • Delivering end-to-end machine learning workflows on Databricks, from data preparation and feature development through training and evaluation to batch and real-time deployment.
  • Maintaining quality in production through versioning, evaluation, monitoring and drift detection, and supporting the investigation and recovery of solutions when issues arise.
  • Collaborating with Product, Engineering, Commercial and Operations teams to translate business needs into scoped technical requirements, measurable success criteria and realistic delivery plans, including relevant data and privacy constraints.
  • Contributing to governance-ready data and AI practices covering quality, lineage, access, security, GDPR and responsible AI, including relevant EU AI Act requirements.
  • Working with technical and non-technical stakeholders to explain trade-offs and model limitations, gather feedback and help prioritize improvements based on their potential impact.
  • Reviewing peer contributions, documenting and sharing knowledge, developing reusable components and helping improve our shared libraries and Data & AI platform tooling.

We would like you to have: 

  • A degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, together with strong English communication skills at C1 level.
  • 3–5 years of hands-on experience in Machine Learning Engineering, Applied AI, Data Science or a related field, including experience taking at least one AI or machine learning solution from prototype into production.
  • Strong Python skills and practical experience with machine learning frameworks such as scikit-learn, PyTorch or equivalent technologies, along with solid SQL and warehouse or lakehouse experience.
  • Hands-on experience with Databricks, including several of the following: Spark, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, MLflow or Workflows.
  • Experience evaluating and deploying models beyond the experimentation stage, with an understanding of monitoring, reliability and production quality.
  • Familiarity with LLM application patterns such as RAG, prompt workflows and evaluation, as well as cloud platforms, ideally AWS, and CI/CD practices for machine learning, or the foundations and motivation to develop further in these areas.
  • The ability to independently deliver well-defined AI/ML tasks, collaborate with product and business stakeholders and explain technical trade-offs, model behavior and limitations to non-technical audiences.

You may ask now, why should I work for you? Let us give you a few reasons – and you'll learn more during the process.

  • A varied and exciting job with a lot of personal responsibility in an international company, where you can develop and expand your skills.
  • Professional and personal development opportunities - incl. personal development budget.
  • Flexible working hours and mobile working.
  • Regular team events and open feedback culture.
  • A versatile field of activity and challenging projects.
  • A supportive and open company culture, providing the opportunity to collaborate with a diverse and professional team.
  • Impact healthcare by accelerating medical innovation through improved access to clinical trials, potentially bringing needed treatments to patients faster.

How to apply & what to expect: 

  • Apply via link (CV only; no cover letter required).
  • Introductory call (30 min) → Technical interview → Take Home Test → Demo Day → Decision.
  • We aim to move promptly and keep you updated at every step. 

At Clariness, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, regardless of race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, disability or age.

For more information, feel free to reach out to

Have we sparked your interest?

Would you like to become part of our dynamic, curious, and international culture with plenty of room for your ideas and creativity in an inspiring atmosphere? If so, we look forward to receiving your application with details of your desired salary and possible starting date, preferably via our application portal.

Clariness GmbH will treat the above information strictly confidential and will especially observe the applicable provisions of the applicable data protection laws. Further information about the use of the applicant data, you will find in the data protection declaration online at https://www.clariness.com/privacy-policy/

title: Software Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
salary_basis: Based on historical internship stipend records at Swarmaero
description_html:
Swarm Aero is redefining air power, building the largest swarming UAV and the most versatile swarming aircraft network in the world. The company is moving quickly to launch the first aircraft designed specifically for swarming, as well as the Command & Control software to mobilize swarms of thousands of heterogeneous autonomous assets and empower human operators to achieve superhuman results.

The team has created and exited multiple startups, negotiated defense deals worth billions of dollars, and designed and built 30+ novel aircraft, with aerospace experience from Scaled Composites, Airbus, Archer Aviation, Blue Origin, and Boom Supersonic.

READ THIS PART FIRST

Legion is not a normal web application. It is command and control software that has to present dense real-time information, coordinate distributed systems, and continue being useful when communications are imperfect.

WHAT WE DO

Swarm Aero is redefining air power. We are building autonomous aircraft and Legion, command and control software designed to coordinate large numbers of heterogeneous autonomous systems. Our team combines experience building novel aircraft, scaling startups, and delivering technology for national security.

THE INTERNSHIP

You will own a scoped project with a clear technical or business outcome, work directly with the people responsible for the system, and present what you built and learned at the end of the summer. The goal is not to give you practice work. It is to give you useful work with the support to do it well.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

· Build product features across frontend, backend, full-stack, real-time, or forward-deployed software

· Develop interfaces for telemetry, geospatial data, mission planning, scheduling, collaboration, or system health

· Build and operate backend services, APIs, event-driven systems, or data pipelines

· Write automated tests, improve developer tooling, and help ship production-quality software

· Support integration and test events, debug issues across services and networks, and turn what you learn into product improvements

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

· Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a closely related field, with graduation and enrollment requirements to be confirmed.

· Strong programming fundamentals and experience building a substantial software project

· Experience with a modern frontend framework, backend language, systems language, or full-stack application

· Ability to explain technical tradeoffs, debug methodically, and write maintainable code

WHAT SETS YOU APART

· React, TypeScript, Go, Python, Rust, C++, or similar tools

· Distributed systems, networking, real-time applications, maps, games, simulation, or data visualization

· Linux, Docker, CI/CD, customer-facing engineering, or deployed project experience

WHAT YOU DO NOT NEED

Aerospace experience, a perfect GPA, or a previous internship at a famous company. Show us what you have built, analyzed, tested, organized, or improved, and be ready to explain your contribution clearly.

THE HONEST VERSION

The pace is fast, the problems will not arrive fully defined, and you may spend part of the summer learning why your first approach was wrong. We will expect you to ask questions, test your assumptions, document your work, and leave the project better than you found it.

ITAR requirement

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Swarm Aero is an equal opportunity employer. We value diverse backgrounds and experiences and make employment decisions without regard to race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, or disability.

What We Offer

  • Meaningful equity in a high-growth defense technology company

  • Competitive base salary commensurate with experience

  • Medical, dental, vision, and 401k

  • PTO and paid sick leave

  • Monthly wellness stipend

  • Daily catered lunch (office)

  • Paid parental leave

  • Direct impact on a critical national security mission

  • A world-class team of engineers and operators solving genuinely hard problems

Compensation: $35 per hour

title: Technical Sourcer
salary_basis: Based on engineering benchmarks at Swarmaero
description_html:
Swarm Aero is redefining air power, building the largest swarming UAV and the most versatile swarming aircraft network in the world. The company is moving quickly to launch the first aircraft designed specifically for swarming, as well as the Command & Control software to mobilize swarms of thousands of heterogeneous autonomous assets and empower human operators to achieve superhuman results.

The team has created and exited multiple startups, negotiated defense deals worth billions of dollars, and designed and built 30+ novel aircraft, with aerospace experience from Scaled Composites, Airbus, Archer Aviation, Blue Origin, and Boom Supersonic.

Read this part first

Somewhere out there is a sourcer who is better than their job title says they are. They hit their numbers at a company that never let them talk to a hiring manager. They found the candidate nobody else found and watched a recruiter take the credit. They have been told to be patient, to wait for the next cycle, to earn it.

We are not going to make you wait.

What we do

We build autonomous aircraft and Legion, the software that flies hundreds of them as one coordinated swarm. Series A, backed by Khosla Ventures, and Coatue. We are hiring software engineers and aircraft engineers at the same time, which is hard, and how fast we hire is one of the few things standing between the current aircraft and the next one.

That is not a motivational line. It is the actual constraint. Recruiting is on the critical path here, and you will be able to see your work in the flight schedule.

The job

You own top of funnel for our software engineering roles: backend, frontend, autonomy, forward deployed. You will be reading GitHub profiles, writing outreach that engineers answer, and building searches that keep producing after the obvious names are gone.

Then the interesting part. Inside your first year you move onto the aircraft side: propulsion, structures, avionics, manufacturing, production. Almost nobody sources both. The people who can are rare enough that it changes what your career looks like from that point forward. We will teach you, and you will be bad at it for a while, and then you will not be.

What you get here that you did not get there

  • Your own reqs, early, with your name on the outcome

  • Hiring managers in the same building, not behind an intake form

  • The freedom to change the message when it is not working, without asking three people first

  • Someone who runs sourcing searches themselves every day and will look at your search strings with you

  • A skill set at the end of two years that maybe a few hundred people in the country have

What we need from you

  • 1+ years of sourcing or recruiting, most of it in software engineering

  • A hire you are proud of, one nobody else was going to find, and the ability to walk us through exactly how you found them

  • A high tolerance for silence, because most of your outreach will go unanswered and the job is making the next message better anyway

  • Real curiosity about how aircraft get built, or at least the honesty to say you find it interesting and want in

  • Writing that sounds like a person, since your entire work product is text a stranger decides to open or delete

  • Clean data habits, because our reporting goes to the CEO and it needs to be right

What we do not need

Ten years of experience. A recruiting pedigree. A degree in anything specific. Permission from your current manager to be good at this.

The honest version

The pace is uncomfortable. You will be asked to fill roles you do not understand yet, and the answer will usually be to go learn them rather than to wait for a briefing.

description_html:
About Genesis AI

Genesis AI builds the simulation platform powering the next generation of robotics and embodied AI. Our flagship product, Genesis World, is a unified multi-physics simulation engine paired with Nyx, our in-house GPU-accelerated, path-traced photorealistic renderer. Together they provide a platform for training robotics and embodied AI at scale; letting teams simulate complex physical worlds with high fidelity and speed, from a laptop to datacenter-grade GPUs, and close the gap between simulation and the real world.

About the Role

A simulator is only as useful as the content that runs inside it. Training embodied agents at scale means large volumes of assets that are simultaneously physically valid and visually convincing and that is a pipeline problem before it is an art problem.

We're hiring a Senior Engineer to build the path from raw input to sim-ready asset: geometry from a range of sources going in; clean meshes, correct collision proxies, plausible physical properties, materials that hold up under a path tracer, and reliable metadata coming out.

The bar is throughput and repeatability. An asset that needs a human pass to be usable doesn't scale, so the pipeline has to make good decisions on its own and flag the cases where it can't.

Part of that autonomy comes from agents embedded in the graph itself. Nodes can call models to produce input content, drive generation, pick parameters, interpret a mesh before deciding how to treat it, or judge whether a result is acceptable. Making that reliable is its own engineering problem: agents are non-deterministic, they fail in ways a mesh operator doesn't, and they need guardrails, structured outputs, retries and verification around them. You'll be building that as a first-class part of the pipeline rather than bolting it on.

You'll work closely with the stakeholders, who set direction and priorities. You own the technical design and the implementation and you're expected to bring enough pipeline experience to challenge the plan where it needs challenging.

What You'll Do

  • Build and maintain the end-to-end asset pipeline, from ingestion through to validated output

  • Design agent-driven nodes that generate input content and make decisions inside the graph, with the structured outputs, guardrails and fallbacks that make them dependable in batch

  • Develop automated processing stages: mesh repair, retopology, decimation and LODs, UV unwrapping and texel density normalization, collision proxy generation

  • Derive physical properties so assets behave correctly in simulation: mass, inertia, contact parameters, articulation setup

  • Handle appearance: material conversion to PBR, texture processing, baking, and color management so assets render correctly in Nyx

  • Define and enforce asset standards (units, orientation, pivots, naming, provenance) and build the validators that reject noncompliant assets before they reach the library

  • Scale the pipeline to large batch runs, with caching, versioning and selective reprocessing when a stage changes

  • Build quality checks into the pipeline itself: physics stability harnesses, render smoke tests, automated evaluation of generated content, comparison on reprocessed assets

  • Work with the rendering, physics and research teams on what sim-ready needs to mean for each downstream use

What We're Looking For (ideally)

  • 5+ years building content or asset pipelines in games, VFX, simulation, or 3D tooling, with ownership of a pipeline in production

  • Deep knowledge of 3D asset formats and their quirks: USD, glTF, FBX, OBJ, plus physics description formats such as URDF or MJCF

  • Strong Python and C++ where processing needs to be fast

  • Hands-on mesh processing expertise: remeshing, decimation, UV generation, repair operations, convex decomposition, and a clear sense of how each one fails

  • Solid command of PBR material authoring, texture baking and color spaces

  • Experience driving DCC tools headlessly (Blender, Houdini, Maya) and building batch or distributed job systems around them

  • Practical experience putting LLM or agent calls into production systems: prompting, tool use, structured output, cost and latency control, and handling non-determinism

  • Understanding of what makes an asset physically valid in a simulator: visual versus collision geometry, mass properties, contact behavior, numerical stability

  • Judgment about quality bars, including when an asset is good enough and when it isn't

Nice to Have

  • Experience processing output from generative or reconstruction-based 3D sources, and evaluating that output automatically

  • Agent frameworks, orchestration and eval tooling applied to content generation

  • OpenUSD at scale: composition, layering, MaterialX

  • Semantic annotation and dataset curation at volume

  • Exposure to simulation stacks such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim or similar

title: Quadrants: Compiler Lead
salary_basis: Based on senior role compensation records at Genesis
description_html:
What Quadrants is

Quadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research.

The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton.

It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public.

The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast.

The role

You own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap.

Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. Getting there is a frontier problem, part research and part engineering, and we intend to define the state of the art on it, relentlessly pushing the limit further.

It calls for two things at once: the low-level GPU and compiler skill to make a single kernel optimal, and the ability to keep the whole system coherent as it grows.

The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX.

Your mandate is to build the best open-source Python compiler for physics simulation out there. No limit on what that takes. If it means replacing the entire engine, your call. Either way, you keep Quadrants healthy and unblocking the company in the meantime.

What you’ll own

  • API & authoring experience. The surface that physics and numerical-computing engineers write against, and, as an open-source library, the product’s face to the world. Idiomatic, natural to Python users, never a separate language bolted onto Python. Clean decorators, legible constraints, sharp errors, real escape hatches.

  • IR, lowering & backends. A stable IR that lowers to multiple backends, with room to grow and the door kept open for differentiable simulation. Today the computation graph is expressed through Quadrants’ own constructs. Recovering it automatically from ordinary Python is hard, and a long-term goal rather than today’s reality.

  • Optimization. Turn naive code into strong execution plans: vectorization, register and shared-memory usage, barriers and atomics, cooperative threading, dead-buffer and redundant-traffic elimination, dropping needless synchronization. Move low-level optimization off users and into the platform.

  • Primitives. Cholesky, eigendecomposition, matmul, reductions, solver kernels. Each owned with its correctness, benchmarks, and regression tracking.

  • Watching Genesis and the compiler together. Hunt for performance wins on both sides, in Genesis and in Quadrants itself. Propose API changes that cut duplication, improve readability, and reduce platform-specific special-casing. Less to maintain, more that simply works.

  • The project as a product. Benchmark real workloads, track performance over time, catch regressions early. Stay close to users (Genesis first), find friction and missing abstractions, drive adoption, set direction.

Who you are

You reason about whole systems and have taste for where complexity should live. You measure before you optimize, and you reach for memory traffic and launch overhead before FLOPs. You have opinions about API design. You write tests and benchmarks as you go, not afterward.

The ground that judgment stands on:

  • GPU. What optimal looks like and why: access patterns, registers, shared memory, barriers, atomics, threading. CPU intuition a plus.

  • Python & API taste. Idiomatic Python. A feel for what’s natural to Python users. APIs that free users rather than constrain them.

  • Compilers. The path from authoring to kernels (IR, lowering, optimization), weighed against maintainability.

And how you work: proactive and largely self-directed. You fetch context across the company instead of waiting for it. You’re comfortable talking to the engineers who use what you build, and at ease designing in the open for users you’ll never meet. Ready to grow into leading a small team (a couple of people, near term).

What great looks like

People adopt Quadrants from outside Genesis. Engineers write clearer code with less boilerplate. Kernels keep getting faster. Performance is tracked, not guessed. The architecture gets easier to extend, not harder.

What we’re uncompromising about

How you work is up to you. What matters is that your ownership grows over time: blind spots shrink, the parts you can vouch for expand, technical debt goes down, the core stays sound.

That takes treating understanding as real work, not overhead. You read and challenge the codebase instead of just stacking features on it. You take nothing you did not write for granted. You watch the competition and what’s coming next, and you bring it in and ship it.

Use AI agents if they help. They are productivity tools, not code owners. You are.

title: Genesis-World: Core Physics Engineer
salary_basis: Based on engineering benchmarks at Genesis
description_html:
What we're building

Robots will learn in simulation before they hit the factory. Genesis-World is our bet on that future.

Genesis-World is an open-source, general-purpose simulation platform for physical AI from Genesis AI. One unified multi-physics engine: rigid bodies, FEM, MPM, particles, cloth, fluids. A robot arm can pour water onto sand, grasp a deformable object, or cut a soft body, all in the same simulation. Nyx, our in-house renderer, may be the most promising renderer for robotics out there: real-time photo-realistic rendering, advanced features like depth of field, and state-of-the-art techniques never seen before. Sensors of every kind: cameras, lidar, IMU, contact forces, temperature, plus arguably the most advanced tactile simulation available (paper). And the engine keeps growing: we are developing internally the most comprehensive and fastest Incremental Potential Contact (paper) solver for deformable body dynamics we know of, soon to be open-sourced. It powers real business applications, from full-fledged box packaging with labelling machine and all, to wire harnessing and lab automation, without any physics hack or compromise.

Everything is Python-first and runs anywhere. Kernels are written once, and Quadrants, our in-house JIT compiler, lowers them to CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, Vulkan, x86, and ARM64. A single laptop or a datacenter. Massively batched GPU simulation for learning at scale, and complex non-batched scenes where CPU wins outright.

This is at the core of Genesis AI's strategy. Evaluation is the bottleneck of scalable robotics: real hardware caps iteration at wall-clock time, but simulation turns it into a compute problem. Ours already runs two orders of magnitude faster than hardware (tens of thousands of episodes in half an hour instead of 200+ hours), while correlating with on-hardware rollouts at 89%. The north star: physical AI that improves at the speed of compute.

The role

You push the physics of Genesis-World forward. The mandate is clear: ship production-ready simulation capabilities that matter for the company's internal needs. Research applied end-to-end, from algorithm to merged, tested, documented code that real robot-learning pipelines depend on. Occasional groundbreaking research happens, notably through academic collaborations. But the core of the job is making the engine measurably better along five axes:

  • Speed. Algorithms that are not only faster but also smart enough to spend compute only where it matters across both time and space: larger stable timesteps, selective fidelity (adaptive across scales or simply hand-set), structure-aware solvers.

  • Completeness. No physics off limits: water, human animation, air flow, gravel, tendons, even body organs. Whatever the next use-case needs, the engine grows to cover it.

  • Fidelity. More realistic models: contact, friction, deformation, energy, actuation, materials…

  • Versatility. Extensible multi-physics without compromise on realism: all solvers in the scene coupled together at once, two-way and constraint-based. Write your own solver and it joins the scene like a native one, growing into an open solver ecosystem.

  • Scalability. From workstation to factory scale, and one day, city scale: thousands of interacting entities, batched across environments, without losing physical soundness.

Our ambition is to establish Genesis-World as the go-to simulator for physical AI, from companies and research labs to individuals.

The problems waiting for you

  • Every fidelity for every physics. The same physics at every point of the speed-accuracy spectrum, from heavily batched training with XPBD or VBD to final validation with IPC. Same scene, same API, pick your tradeoff.

  • Invent physics level-of-detail (LOD). Rendering has had LOD for decades, physics is still waiting. Simulate at full fidelity what agents interact with and see, coarsely what they do not.

  • Heterogeneous environments. Every parallel world can hold a completely different model: different bodies, joints, and collision geometries.

  • Adaptive timesteps per island. Error-based control with Runge-Kutta Dopri5, and Time-of-Impact stepping during collision detection, as done in Jiminy.

  • Couple everything, exactly. Efficient and accurate two-way constraint-based coupling between heterogeneous grey-box solvers, using state-of-the-art methods like ADMM. Owning every solver in the stack is what makes it possible.

  • More scalable constraint solvers. Push rigid constraint solving beyond its current scalability ceiling (reference).

  • Unify contact resolution. Hydro-elastic compliance, unilateral constraints, and sequential impulses in the same framework, ideally under one generic formulation.

  • Closed kinematic loops without constraints. Handle loops intrinsically for numerical stability and speed, in the spirit of Kamino.

Day to day: you write your physics in plain Python and Quadrants makes it fast on every backend. And you validate it the hard way: analytical closed forms, other engines, real-world data.

Who you are

You are a physicist and an engineer at once. You judge a method by whether it holds up in production at real scale, and you do not stop until it does. No blind spots: you relentlessly hunt down even the defect that looks insignificant, because it never is.

  • A strong background in physics-based simulation, preferably related to robotics: RBD, FEM, MPM, SPH, IPC, XPBD, VBD, ABD, plus constrained optimization and numerical integration of stiff systems.

  • A track record of shipping simulation code that others rely on, in an engine, in industry, or in a research codebase used beyond its authors.

  • Solid HPC programming (CPU and/or GPU), and an instinct for what makes a numerical method fast in practice, beyond complexity classes.

  • Rigor in validation: analytical closed forms, cross-engine consistency, real-world data.

Bonus points: publications in simulation, graphics, or robotics venues (SIGGRAPH, ICRA, IROS, CoRL, RSS). Contributions to an open-source physics engine.

The north star: physical AI that improves at the speed of compute.

The role

Simulation is still a hard sell in robotics. Outside a few success stories, like reinforcement learning for locomotion, most teams skip it, and friction is a big part of why: painful to use, painful to debug. We live that pain ourselves: debugging a failing experiment during policy evaluation takes 30 minutes, and there is no way to automatically generate a standalone reproduction script. That blocks adoption, even internally.

Your job is to kill that friction. You build the software engineering backbone of Genesis-World: everything that makes a large, fast-moving simulation codebase reliable, maintainable, frictionless. And it all ships in the open. Every hour of pain you remove, you remove for every roboticist who comes after you.

You join as core maintainer of Genesis-World, with shared stewardship of the whole platform from day one. Our physics team develops the algorithms, but just as importantly, you work to make everything around them excellent: infrastructure, tooling, APIs, architecture.

The problems waiting for you

  • Make testing of a JIT-compiled engine scalable. Running our full suite is already taking hours because the ratio between compile time and runtime can be as bad as x10. Getting rid of this bottleneck is a serious challenge that will require a joint effort from the Genesis-World and the compiler teams.

  • Make any bug reproducible. Dump and reload simulations bit-exactly, across machines, across backends, even when a single timestep of a batched simulation can already max out VRAM. Turn any failing run into a standalone reproduction script, automatically.

  • Make autodiff first-class. Genesis-World is differentiable today, but partially: memory-hungry, slower than it could be, and hard to maintain due to manual operation recording. The project spans the engine and the compiler: you drive the requirements on Quadrants and iterate in a tight loop with the compiler team until the integration is solid.

  • Edit scenes at frozen time. See the scene, move entities and robots around, iterate on layout, all without building the scene or compiling the engine. Authoring today means a full build cycle. Make it instant.

  • Make the simulator extensible. First-class plugins for physics solvers and interactive viewer backends, including Nyx. Sensors already work this way. Generalize it, and Genesis-World becomes a platform others build on.

  • Give robots real actuation. Motors and MIMO transmissions, cleanly abstracted at the interface between users and the physics engine.

  • Make time a local variable. Today the clock and the timestep are global to the engine, which forbids whole classes of speedups: environments cannot step independently, the timestep cannot adapt to the state, and individual solvers cannot advance at their own rate. Free the clock down to the sub-scene level and let the simulation fly.

  • Make scenes come alive. Events triggered by physics: press the button and the microwave door pops open, squeeze the trigger and the drill spins.

  • Keep the core sharp. Refactoring legacy subsystems, stronger typing, consistent coding style, less Python overhead on hot paths, full scene serialization, telemetry and replay.

Beyond the code: you review issues and pull requests with the core team, answer questions from users and contributors, and can join the push on adoption.

Who you are

You care about the engineer using what you build as much as the thing itself. A slow test, a cryptic error, a manual step: you see it, you go after the root cause, and you remove it for everyone. You have opinions about API design.

You are comfortable with physics and robotics: the right design choices take a working picture of what a simulator like Genesis-World does, how it works, and how it is used, a picture you can partly build on the job.

  • Strong Python engineering on large codebases: architecture, refactoring, typing, packaging, performance profiling (py-spy, Nsight, Xcode Instruments, RenderDoc).

  • Developer tooling, test infrastructure, or CI at scale.

  • Enough fluency with JIT compilation, code generation, or GPU computing stacks to reason about compilation caching, kernel dispatch, and startup cost. You will work closely with Quadrants.

  • At ease debugging across the full platform matrix: Windows, Linux, and macOS, on x86 and arm64, over CUDA, AMD, and Apple Metal (and possibly Intel XPU via Vulkan soon)

  • Open-source reflexes: triaging issues, reviewing external pull requests, communicating with a community.

Bonus points: experience with other robotics simulators (Drake, MuJoCo, Newton, Isaac, RaiSim, Jiminy, Brax). PyTorch, our user-facing interface. Other JIT compilers such as Triton, JAX, or Numba. 3D tooling and interactive editors (Maya, Blender, Houdini). Serialization formats (USD, glTF, MJCF/URDF). C++, CUDA, or Metal. Developer relations or community work.

About the Role
Genesis AI is building Genesis World, a unified multi-physics simulation engine paired with Nyx, our in-house path traced photorealistic renderer that powers the next generation of robotics and embodied AI. We are looking for a Senior Prop Artist to model, sculpt, and texture the physical objects and digital twins that populate our simulated worlds. Because these assets are used as training data for machines operating in the physical world, close enough is not enough, meaning scale, proportion, material response, and geometric accuracy must all hold up under scrutiny. This is a craft heavy role where you will apply game caliber art skills beyond entertainment to build beautiful, efficient assets that perform in real time and directly narrow the gap between simulation and reality.

What You'll Do

  • Create photoreal props for digital twins end-to-end: modeling, high-poly sculpting, retopology, UVs, and PBR texturing.

  • Recreate real-world objects from reference and photogrammetry, matching real dimensions, materials, and wear.

  • Clean up, retopologize, and optimize scanned and existing assets to meet real-time budgets without losing fidelity.

  • Author assets to strict poly, texture, and memory budgets suited to GPU-accelerated real-time rendering.

  • Partner with rendering and physics engineers to make sure assets are visually and physically correct in-engine.

  • Maintain consistency, naming, and quality standards across a growing library of props.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years as a prop / hard-surface / environment artist, with shipped work built under AAA real-time engine constraints (games, not VFX).

  • Strong modeling skills in Maya and/or Blender and sculpting expertise in ZBrush.

  • Mastery of PBR texturing in Substance (Painter/Designer).

  • Photogrammetry and scan cleanup experience; comfortable turning raw scans into production-ready assets.

  • Deep understanding of real-time constraints: poly budgets, LODs, texture memory, and optimization tradeoffs.

  • A sharp eye for accuracy, scale, and material fidelity, and the discipline to hit them consistently.

Nice to Have

  • Familiarity with real-time / GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines and how assets behave in a path-traced renderer.

  • Interest or background in robotics, embodied AI, or sim-to-real.

Genesis AI is building Nyx, a renderer that delivers offline quality at realtime performance, powered by next generation capture and rendering technology built on light fields and Gaussian splatting. Nice to have

title: Strategic Account Executive - France
salary_basis: Based on engineering benchmarks at Rescale
description_html:
France-based | French required | English required | Additional languages are a plus | Approximately 30% travel

About Rescale

Rescale is pioneering the future of engineering and scientific discovery. As the leader in digital engineering, we help the world’s most advanced organizations develop better products faster through intelligent automation, applied AI, data management, and access to the world’s largest network of engineering and R&D applications.

Rescale brings together elastic, enterprise-grade HPC with advanced modeling and simulation, agentic engineering, AI Physics, and the software and data workflows that connect them. Our customers use Rescale to modernize R&D, accelerate simulation, automate engineering processes, and turn engineering data into faster, better decisions across industries including automotive, manufacturing, aerospace, energy, life sciences, and semiconductors.

Joining Rescale means becoming part of a diverse, collaborative, and mission-driven team solving complex challenges that traditional HPC alone cannot address.

The Role

We are looking for a high-performing Strategic Account Executive to lead direct enterprise sales and account growth across France.

This is an entrepreneurial, field-based role focused on building and expanding strategic relationships with key and enterprise accounts. You will own a defined portfolio of named accounts, create demand, develop executive relationships, win new business, and expand Rescale’s footprint from foundational HPC into advanced modeling and simulation, agentic engineering, and AI Physics.

You will operate as the commercial owner of your territory: setting the account strategy, identifying business problems, building internal champions, creating compelling value cases, and leading complex sales cycles from first engagement through renewal and expansion. This is a direct-sales role, not a channel-led position. You will work closely with Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Marketing, Sales Development, Product, and Rescale leadership, while retaining ownership of the commercial strategy and outcome.

France is a priority market, with particular emphasis on automotive and manufacturing enterprises where engineering organizations are investing in digital engineering transformation. Success requires the ability to sell both into existing strategic relationships and into new enterprise accounts where Rescale can create meaningful business impact.

What You’ll Do

  • Own and grow a focused portfolio of strategic key and enterprise accounts across France.

  • Build account and territory plans that identify the highest-value expansion paths, whitespace, executive relationships, and competitive risks.

  • Expand existing Rescale customers by introducing additional capabilities across the platform, from Rescale HPC to Advanced Modeling and Simulation, Agentic Engineering, and AI Physics.

  • Develop new enterprise relationships and win new logos where Rescale’s platform can transform engineering and R&D workflows.

  • Generate pipeline through proactive prospecting, account-based engagement, executive networking, customer insight, and disciplined market development.

  • Engage senior stakeholders across engineering, R&D, simulation, IT, digital transformation, finance, procurement, and executive leadership.

  • Lead the full enterprise sales cycle, including account planning, discovery, qualification, value engineering, business-case development, solution alignment, negotiation, procurement, and close.

  • Position Rescale as a strategic platform for HPC modernization, simulation acceleration, engineering workflow transformation, and AI-driven product development.

  • Articulate how Rescale’s offerings work together: HPC as the scalable foundation; Advanced Modeling and Simulation as the workflow layer; Agentic Engineering as the automation layer; and AI Physics as the intelligence layer that turns simulation data into predictive insight.

  • Build trusted relationships across the customer organization, from end users and technical champions to business sponsors, procurement leaders, and C-level decision-makers.

  • Orchestrate internal teams to deliver coordinated account plans, executive engagement, technical validation, pilots, and commercial proposals.

  • Maintain rigorous Salesforce hygiene, forecast accuracy, opportunity inspection, and pipeline coverage, with clear weekly visibility into commit, likely, best case, and risk.

  • Represent Rescale in customer meetings, industry events, and executive forums across France, with travel expected at approximately 30%.

What Success Looks Like

  • Consistent achievement and overachievement of quarterly and annual revenue targets through a healthy mix of account expansion and net-new enterprise business.

  • Durable growth within strategic accounts, including broader adoption of Rescale’s platform and expansion into new teams, workloads, geographies, and use cases.

  • A high-quality, self-generated pipeline across automotive, manufacturing, and other engineering-intensive industries.

  • New enterprise logos and meaningful strategic wins in the French market.

  • Executive-level credibility with customers navigating HPC modernization, simulation, AI, and digital engineering transformation.

  • Clear customer value cases that connect technical outcomes to business priorities such as faster product development, higher engineering productivity, improved infrastructure flexibility, and better R&D economics.

  • Consistent operating discipline, urgency, ownership, resilience, and transparency in a high-growth environment.

Who You Are

  • An entrepreneurial enterprise seller who creates opportunity rather than waiting for inbound demand.

  • Equally comfortable expanding an established strategic account and opening a new enterprise relationship.

  • A strong hunter with the persistence and commercial judgment to create access, build consensus, and win competitive deals.

  • Confident engaging technical practitioners while earning credibility with senior business leaders and executives.

  • Resilient and resourceful in long, complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles.

  • Commercially disciplined and accountable for your number, account strategy, forecast, pipeline quality, and execution.

  • Consultative, curious, and able to translate complex technology into compelling business outcomes.

  • Collaborative and low-ego, with the influence to mobilize cross-functional teams without losing ownership of the result.

  • Motivated by the opportunity to help define a new category at the intersection of cloud HPC, digital engineering, automation, and AI.

Key Qualifications

  • 5+ years of success in enterprise or strategic account sales, ideally selling complex technical, cloud, SaaS, platform, engineering, or scientific-computing solutions.

  • Demonstrated success growing enterprise accounts and/or winning new business in France.

  • Experience selling to large organizations in automotive, manufacturing, industrial technology, engineering software, simulation, HPC, cloud, or adjacent technology environments.

  • A track record of managing long, complex, multi-threaded enterprise sales cycles from discovery through close and expansion.

  • Ability to engage credibly with engineering, R&D, IT, digital transformation, procurement, finance, and executive stakeholders.

  • Strong skills in consultative discovery, value selling, negotiation, executive communication, and closing.

  • Experience using Salesforce or a similar CRM with disciplined opportunity management and forecasting.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in French and English. Additional languages are an advantage.

  • Strong organization, prioritization, and account-planning skills.

  • Must be based in France and able to travel regularly to customer sites and industry events across the country.

Why Rescale

Rescale serves many of the world’s most advanced engineering organizations and is helping define the next generation of digital engineering. For the right sales leader, this is an opportunity to shape strategic accounts in a category where cloud HPC, advanced simulation, agentic engineering, and AI Physics are converging to change how products are designed, tested, and brought to market.

If you are energized by building executive relationships, creating demand, expanding strategic accounts, and helping engineering organizations move from traditional infrastructure and fragmented workflows to an intelligent digital engineering platform, this role offers significant strategic and commercial upside.

Rescale is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all qualified persons regardless of race, sex, disability, religion or belief, sexual orientation, age, or any other protected characteristic. Employment with Rescale is contingent upon successful completion of a comprehensive background check. For details on the information Rescale collects during the application process, please see the Applicant Privacy Notice.

description_html:
Internship - Total Rewards (Compensation & Benefits)

About Ledger

We’re a team of experts pushing the limits of what’s possible, united by our common goal to unlock true freedom through digital ownership, making technology accessible for all. We believe in a world where users, creators and enterprises manage their value with ownership and freedom. Our curiosity drives us to innovate, empowering individuals on a global scale. We believe change is constant and our team moves forward as one, with a culture of problem-solving where every employee is empowered and supported to challenge tradition and create solutions. Our mission is simple: to make self-custody accessible and give people the keys to their own financial futures. If you want to make a true impact, we want you to join us at Ledger.

At Ledger, we’re proud to be the global platform for digital assets and Web3, with over 20% of the world’s crypto assets secured through our Ledger devices. With our headquarters in Paris, and offices in Vierzon, Grenoble, Montpellier, London, Portland, Geneva, Zurich and Central Singapore, we have a team of around 600 professionals developing a variety of products and services to enable individuals and companies to securely buy, store, swap, grow and manage crypto assets – including the Ledger hardware wallets line with more than 7.5 millions units already sold in 200 countries.

The Team

Working closely with the Head of Total Rewards (London-based) and the Compensation & Benefits Expert (Paris-based), this role offers a unique combination of business-as-usual (BAU) operational and process management along with high-impact strategic project and analytical work.

What You’ll Be Doing:

Pay Equity Analytics

  • Pay Equity Modeling: Own the quantitative data preparation, variance testing, and baseline modeling for internal pay equity audits and gender pay gap analysis.

  • EU Directive Alignment: Actively support the team’s preparations for the upcoming EU Pay Transparency Directive by leveraging statistical analysis to identify and report on compensation trends across employee cohorts.

Equity Platform Dashboards & Maintenance

  • Grant List Creation & Validation: Prepare, audit, and validate equity grant lists, ensuring absolute accuracy before final approvals. Partner directly with HR Ops and Legal teams to deliver clean, compliant data for new equity grants.

  • Equity Tracking: Explore the creation of analytical dashboards/trackers to monitor global equity distribution, vesting schedules, and dilution tracking (e.g., BSPCE, Stock Options).

C&B Operations

  • Annual Review Support: Help run the operational backbone of our annual compensation review cycles (merit, performance, bonus) by managing data templates, tracking timelines, and coordinating with HRBPs.

  • Survey Submissions & Benchmarking: Coordinate and execute global compensation and benefits survey submissions, ensuring clean data mapping, and perform basic market benchmarking to support pay positioning decisions.

  • Patent Premiums Administration: Operationalize and administer our global patent/invention premiums, partnering closely with the Intellectual Property (IP) and Payroll teams to ensure seamless execution.

  • Workday Data Maintenance: Own the quarterly data upload process in Workday, ensuring all miscellaneous payroll bonus data is accurately tracked and updated on time.

What We’re Looking For

  • Education: Pursuing a Master’s degree in a highly quantitative discipline (e.g., Corporate Finance, Statistics, Financial Engineering, Business Analytics, Data Science, or Econometrics).

  • Advanced Mathematical Analytics: High mathematical baseline with strong capabilities in statistical modeling, variance tracking, and processing complex datasets. Advanced, robust Excel is a baseline requirement.

  • AI Tooling & Agentic Workflows (Strong Plus): Hands-on experience or deep curiosity regarding AI agents and workflow automation. Ideally, you know how to leverage tools like Claude and Gemini beyond basic prompting.

  • Execution & Balance: Adaptable and resourceful in a fast-paced, multicultural environment, proactive rather than reactive.

  • Languages: Fluent in English; French is a plus.

Context & Purpose of the Role

The Total Rewards team is entering a high-intensity period: a year-end compensation review cycle, active benchmarking work, custom bonus plan reviews, and a rising volume of analytical deliverables supporting executive and board-level reporting. To protect bandwidth and quality, we are bringing in a mid-level contractor to work closely with and under the supervision of our Paris-based Compensation & Benefits Expert, reporting directly to the Head of Total Rewards. This is a hands-on, execution-focused role for someone with genuine C&B grounding who can work with light direction once context is set, and who understands what makes compensation data credible.

What You'll Be Working On

Year-End Compensation Review

  • Support data preparation and validation for the annual merit, performance, and bonus review cycles: building and maintaining population files, tracking timelines, and flagging data quality issues before they become problems.

  • Work closely with the C&B Expert on modelling and scenario analysis (budget impact, distribution curves, outlier identification), producing clean, auditable outputs.

  • Contribute to salary budget modelling and refresh of salary structures using latest market data, including updates to merit matrices.

  • Coordinate with HRBPs and People Ops on data collection and sign-off workflows to keep the cycle on track.

Analytical Work for Board & Executive Reporting

  • On direction from the Head of Total Rewards, carry out the underlying data pulls, analysis, and cross-checks to populate compensation metrics and summaries used in board and executive slides.

  • Produce clean, presentation-ready tables and data panels with accurate footnotes and sourcing, so outputs can be directly incorporated into slide decks.

Bonus Plan Design Reviews

  • This contractor may provide support to the C&B Expert and Head of Total Rewards during bonus plan reviews, including

    • Preparing and updating slide decks to support design discussions.

    • Running employee data analyses and refreshing payout range modelling for plan redesigns.

    • Using AI tools to update bonus plan rules documentation in Word as designs evolve, ensuring plan write-ups accurately reflect agreed changes ahead of final review.

Ad Hoc C&B Support

  • Support the C&B Expert on operational tasks: Workday data uploads, equity grant list preparation and validation, and patent premium tracking.

  • Support the C&B Expert and Head of Total Rewards on ad hoc projects. Examples may include aspects of job architecture and related market benchmarking analytics, pay equity & equity grant modelling.

What We're Looking For

Requirement

Experience

4 years+ in Compensation & Benefits or Total Rewards. C&B-specific experience is required; broader HR analytics backgrounds without meaningful C&B exposure will not be considered.

Education

Degree in a quantitative discipline preferred (e.g. Finance, Economics, Statistics, or equivalent).

Excel & Modelling

Advanced Excel is non-negotiable: pivot tables, scenario modelling, audit-proof workbooks, and confident handling of large datasets.

Benchmarking Tools

Hands-on experience with Radford or Mercer Comptryx strongly preferred. Familiarity with the mechanics of job matching and market data interpretation is expected.

Workday

Experience using Workday for compensation cycle management is a strong plus.

Stakeholder Exposure

Experience working with or supporting stakeholders outside France — whether across European markets or globally — is a plus.

Autonomy

Able to work from a defined brief with minimal hand-holding. Asks the right clarifying questions early; doesn't need ongoing supervision once context is clear.

Languages

Fluent English required (working language of the team). French strongly preferred — most day-to-day collaborators are Paris-based.

Tools

Comfort with AI tools (e.g. Claude, Gemini) for document drafting and workflow efficiency is welcome.

What This Role Is (and Isn't)

This is not a strategy or design role — Ledger already has senior expertise in-house for that. What we need is someone who executes cleanly and independently at the analytical and operational level, and who brings enough C&B literacy to produce outputs that don't need to be re-done. You will be working on real, high-stakes deliverables from day one.
